title: We used each other, they will say. The deal ends badly.
subtitle: Jinn and their human followers gathered on the Day
then: Ibn Jurayj said that before Islam a traveler would arrive in a valley and say: {trap}I seek refuge with the master jinn of this valley.{/trap} Al-Hasan said they benefited from each other: the jinn commanded and the humans obeyed. On the Day, that arrangement is exposed, and {trap}it ends in the Fire{/trap}, except as Allah wills.
now: A friendship built on covering for each other. A business partner who helps you cut corners while you help him. {trap}It feels like mutual benefit.{/trap} {idea}Ask where the arrangement is taking both of you.{/idea}
old: As long as we both get something out of it, the relationship is fine.
new: A partnership in wrong is not a benefit. It is a shared road to loss.
try: Think of one relationship where you enable each other's worst habits. Change your part of it.

title: Wrongdoers end up with wrongdoers as their allies.
subtitle: The company you keep is earned
then: Qatadah said wrongdoers become allies of each other, following one another into the Fire. Ibn Zayd recited {trap}whoever turns from the remembrance of the Merciful, We assign him a devil as companion.{/trap} Ibn Kathir adds that Allah also {trap}sets wrongdoers over one another{/trap}, as a just result.
now: You start lying at work and suddenly your lunch group is the people who lie best. You start gossiping and the gossips find you. {idea}Your deeds shape your circle.{/idea} The good news: it works the other way too.
old: My friends just happened. They have nothing to do with how I live.
new: The company I keep follows the deeds I choose. I can change both.
try: Spend some time this week with one person whose habits you want to grow into.

title: Did messengers not come to you? Yes, we admit it.
subtitle: The world's glitter deceived them, and they confess

row.title: we were distracted
sub: by the glitter of this life

then: On the Day, jinn and humans are asked: {idea}did messengers not come to you, reciting My verses and warning you of this Day?{/idea} They admit it. Ibn Kathir says {trap}they were deceived by the beauty, adornment and desires of this life{/trap}, and wasted their lives rejecting what came.
now: Your phone has a Quran app, a dozen lectures saved, a friend who reminds you. No one can say they were not told. {trap}The danger is not ignorance. It is distraction.{/trap} {idea}You already know enough to act on something.{/idea}
old: I will take faith seriously once I learn more.
new: I have already been reminded. The question is whether the world is distracting me.
try: Act today on one thing you already know you should do, instead of learning something new.

title: No town is destroyed before it is warned.
subtitle: Allah's justice: the message always comes first

row.title: warning first
sub: no one is left without excuse

then: Ibn Kathir explains that Allah sent messengers and books so that {idea}no one could say they were punished without being told.{/idea} He cites: {reward}We never punish until We have sent a messenger{/reward}, and every nation had a warner. The Makkans were hearing their warning right then.
now: Your manager gives you a written warning before any firing. You still feel it was unfair. {idea}Allah is more just than any manager.{/idea} Every reminder you receive is part of that warning, given out of mercy.
old: Allah might punish me for things I was never told about.
new: Allah always warns before He holds anyone to account. His reminders are mercy.
try: Think of a recent reminder you received. Thank Allah for the warning and respond to it.

title: Everyone gets a level matching what they did.
subtitle: Degrees for each, and nothing missed
then: At-Tabari said everyone who obeys or disobeys has {idea}ranks according to their works{/idea}, good for good and evil for evil. Ibn Jarir adds that all they did, {reward}your Lord was aware of and recorded{/reward}, to repay them when they return to Him.
now: You hold the door for someone. You hold your tongue in an argument. No one claps. {reward}None of it is lost.{/reward} {idea}Each small choice moves you up or down a level{/idea} with a Lord who never looks away.
old: Small good deeds do not really count for much.
new: Every deed builds my level, and my Lord does not miss any of it.
try: Do one small kindness today that no one will see, and leave it with Allah.

title: He needs nothing from you, and He is full of mercy.
subtitle: He could replace you, as you replaced others
then: Ibn Kathir explains Al-Ghani as {idea}free of needing His creatures in any way{/idea}, while they need Him in every situation. He is also {reward}full of mercy{/reward}. If they defy Him, He can bring others in their place, as He raised them from the offspring of earlier people.
now: Some days you pray like you are doing Allah a favor. Then you notice how many generations lived in your house, your street, before you. {idea}He does not need you. He wants good for you.{/idea} That is what mercy looks like.
old: My prayers and good deeds are something Allah needs from me.
new: Allah needs nothing from me. My worship is for my own good, and His mercy surrounds me.
try: Before your next prayer, remind yourself: I am the one who needs this.

title: What you are promised is coming, and no one escapes it.
subtitle: The Resurrection is certain
then: The Prophet ﷺ is told to say that what they were promised {idea}will surely come{/idea}, meaning the Resurrection. Ibn Kathir says {trap}they cannot escape{/trap}, for Allah is able to bring them back even after they turn to dust and bones.
now: You plan your retirement down to the year. Your holiday is booked months ahead. {idea}The one appointment that is truly certain{/idea} gets the least planning. Give it a slot in your thinking.
old: The Day of Judgment is far away and not worth planning for.
new: It is certainly coming. I can prepare for it like any real appointment.
try: Write down one thing you want to have done before you meet Allah, and take one step on it.

title: Keep doing your thing. I will keep doing mine. Time will tell.
subtitle: A calm challenge from the Prophet ﷺ
then: Ibn Abbas explained the phrase as {idea}your way{/idea}: stay on your way if you think it is right, and I will stay on mine. Ibn Kathir says Allah kept His promise. {reward}The Prophet ﷺ later entered Makkah and his message spread across Arabia{/reward} in his lifetime.
now: Your family thinks your prayer, your modest choices, your refusal of the shady deal are naive. You do not need to win the argument tonight. {idea}Keep working your way, quietly and well.{/idea} The end will show.
old: I have to convince everyone right now that I am right.
new: I can keep doing what is right calmly, and let the end show who was right.
try: The next time someone mocks a good choice of yours, smile, keep going, and say nothing.

title: A share for Allah, a share for the idols, and they cheated.
subtitle: Dividing what Allah created between Him and partners
then: Ibn Abbas described it: they set aside part of their crops for Allah and part for the idol. If anything from Allah's share fell into the idol's, {trap}they kept it there, saying the idol is poor.{/trap} If the idol's share spilled into Allah's, they took it back. {idea}Evil is how they judge.{/idea}
now: You set aside an hour for Quran and an hour for TV. The Quran hour gets eaten by emails. The TV hour never does. {trap}Allah's share always shrinks first.{/trap} Notice which side wins when things collide.
old: I give Allah His share of my time and money. That is enough.
new: Everything I have is His. And when time collides, His share should not be the first to go.
try: Protect one small slot today for Allah that nothing else is allowed to take.

title: Their partners made even killing their children seem right.
subtitle: How fear and custom can disguise a terrible wrong

picture.label: How it was made to look fair

then: Ibn Kathir says the devils {trap}made it seem fair to kill their children for fear of poverty{/trap}, and to bury daughters for fear of dishonor. As-Suddi said it was to destroy them and confuse their religion. {idea}Allah disliked these practices{/idea}, and tells the Prophet ﷺ to leave them with their fabrications.
now: Fear of money, fear of what people say. These still push parents to choices that hurt their kids: never home, always angry, pressure that crushes. {trap}Fear can make something harmful look like responsibility.{/trap} {idea}Look at your children with the eyes of mercy.{/idea}
old: Whatever I do out of fear for my family's future must be right.
new: Fear can make harm look reasonable. I check my choices with Allah's mercy.
try: Spend fifteen minutes today fully with a child in your life, phone away.

title: They made their own forbidden lists and called them Allah's.
subtitle: Invented taboos on cattle and crops
then: Ibn Abbas and others said these were animals they had declared forbidden, like the Bahirah and Wasilah. Qatadah called it {trap}a prohibition the devils set on their wealth, extremism that did not come from Allah.{/trap} They pinned it on Allah's religion. {idea}He never allowed or approved it.{/idea}
now: Someone in your family insists you cannot do something, wear something, say something, "because it is religion." No source, just habit. {trap}Adding rules can be as false as removing them.{/trap} {idea}Ask where it comes from.{/idea}
old: Being stricter than needed is always safer.
new: Inventing rules and calling them Allah's is a lie against Him, even when it looks pious.
try: Pick one strict rule you follow. Find out this week whether it is from Allah or from habit.

title: Good for our men, forbidden to our women, unless it died.
subtitle: Unfair rules women carried in the name of religion
then: Ibn Abbas said this was about milk and newborn animals: {trap}the men got them, the women did not, unless the animal was born dead{/trap}, then they all shared. Allah forbade it. Mujahid and others said He will repay them {idea}for what their tongues falsely described{/idea} as lawful and forbidden.
now: At family gatherings the men eat first and the women get what is left. Someone says it is just how religious families do it. {trap}Unfairness wrapped in religion is still unfairness.{/trap} {idea}Allah is wise and knows what is really being done.{/idea}
old: If it is an old custom, it must be part of the faith.
new: Allah condemned customs that favored men in His name. He sees through the label.
try: At the next family meal, make sure someone who is usually served last gets served first.

title: They lost: their children, their provision, and the truth.
subtitle: Foolishness without knowledge, and what it cost
then: Ibn Abbas said: {trap}if you want to know how ignorant the Arabs were, recite the verses after one hundred and thirty in Al-An'am.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says they lost this life by harming their children and restricting their own wealth, and the next by {trap}lying about Allah.{/trap}
now: You make big decisions on rumors, a cousin's advice, a viral post. Then you defend them as if Allah commanded them. {idea}Foolishness is acting without knowledge.{/idea} Learning first protects your family and your faith.
old: I know enough to make religious decisions for my family on my own.
new: Acting on religion without knowledge cost people everything. I learn before I decide.
try: Before your next big family decision, ask someone knowledgeable and trustworthy first.
